accepted_concepts.label: Chessboard Covering Problem with Backtracking
accepted_concepts.description: The problem is to place the 8 non-pawn pieces on a chessboard such that every square is threatened. The search uses an array of 8 piece position indices, and can be pruned by placing pieces in order of decreasing power and checking if the remaining pieces can cover the remaining holes.
coverage_criteria: Student can define the covering problem.
Student can describe the representation and candidate construction.
Student can explain the pruning condition: total_max_coverage(remaining_pieces) < uncovered_squares => backtrack.
accepted_concepts.merge_rationale: This candidate fully captures the backtracking approach to the chessboard covering problem with pruning techniques.

accepted_concepts.label: Bandwidth Problem and Backtracking
accepted_concepts.description: Defines the bandwidth optimization problem: given a graph, find a linear ordering of vertices that minimizes the maximum length of an edge. A naive solution enumerates all n! permutations and checks the maximum edge span. Backtracking can prune the search by comparing against the current best bandwidth.
coverage_criteria: Student can state the bandwidth problem and compute bandwidth for a small example.
Student can explain why a brute-force search over all permutations is inefficient and that it is NP-hard.
Student can outline how a backtracking solver would be structured using permutation generation with pruning.
accepted_concepts.merge_rationale: These candidates together cover the problem definition, contest context, and backtracking application for the bandwidth problem.

accepted_concepts.label: Recognizing Exhaustive Problems for Backtracking
accepted_concepts.description: Problems that ask to generate or compute all possibilities (e.g., 'generate all subsets', 'compute all permutations') often signal that backtracking is applicable.
coverage_criteria: Given a set of problem statements, identify which ones are suitable for backtracking based on keywords like 'generate all' or 'compute all'.
accepted_concepts.merge_rationale: This candidate provides a heuristic for identifying problems suitable for backtracking.
